punchline: Doctors handed a bag of candy they didn't even eat reached the right diagnosis faster.
thirty_sec: Shawn Achor argues against 'work hard, succeed, then be happy,' because every success just moves the goalpost. He points to a review of 225 studies and over 275,000 people linking happiness to later success. One example: 44 doctors read the same patient file, and half got a small bag of candy first. They didn't eat it. The ones in a good mood still reached the right diagnosis earlier. For Achor, happiness works best as fuel at the start.
